# Review contract

Verification backends read this file: they receive it alongside the diff and are asked to name the principle a finding violates. Ordinary coding sessions do not read it.

A finding names the principle it violates. Name it and judge severity independently: the class governs blocking only, and it never lowers what you reported. A `blocking` class ADDS blocking to a finding already at critical or major severity. `major` and `suggestion` add nothing and leave your own decision untouched, so a finding the reviewer blocked on still blocks. `correctness` is a seventh value a finding may name and it blocks like security; it is the floor beneath the six, not one of them. Once capping is enabled, a finding inside this contract that names no principle is capped at suggestion.

## Outside this contract

accessibility, performance, data-safety

## Coherence

The change fits the design it lands in: one concept has one home, and new code follows the boundaries and data flow the project already has.

Violations: a second copy of an existing abstraction; logic placed in a layer the project keeps it out of; a reverse dependency between modules; a suggested ruling that applies and is not cited.

Blocking: major

## Uniformity

Same things look the same: naming, error shapes, file layout, and interfaces match the project's existing patterns.

Violations: a new naming scheme beside the existing one; an error returned where the project throws; a hand-rolled utility where a shared one exists.

Blocking: major

## Maintainability

The next reader can change it safely: intent is stated where it is not obvious, and the change is no larger or more coupled than its job requires.

Violations: a load-bearing decision with no recorded reason; a function that needs the whole file read to be changed; dead or duplicated paths left behind.

Blocking: major

## Robustness

The code behaves under the inputs and failures it will actually meet: bounds, absence, concurrency, partial failure, restart.

Violations: an unbounded read or loop; an absent value treated as zero; a write with no durability barrier where one is expected; a resource not released on the failure path.

Blocking: blocking

## Security

No new way for untrusted input or a less trusted party to act with more authority than intended.

Violations: unvalidated external input reaching a command, query, path, or privileged call; secrets or credentials in code or logs; a permission or sandbox setting widened without an explicit decision.

Blocking: blocking

## Quality

The change is verified to do what it claims: tests exist for the behaviour, they fail without the change, and the claim in the description matches what shipped.

Violations: a test that passes with the change removed; a green suite over code that is never executed; a description that names work the diff does not contain; a grep transcript in EXISTING.

Blocking: major

## Notes on this file

Ordering is load-bearing. The lens backend receives only the first 3000 characters of this file, head-truncated, so the six principles stay above anything this project adds. A principle pushed below that line is one a lens reviewer is asked to name without ever being shown it.

The "Outside this contract" line is read literally. Every line under that heading is split on commas and newlines into entries, trailing punctuation is stripped, and a `- ` bullet prefix is NOT stripped, so a bulleted entry matches nothing and prose written there becomes junk entries. One plain comma-separated line, or nothing at all. Entries are matched against a finding's category and, for a merged lens finding, against every contributing lens id.

A finding outside the contract is never capped and keeps the severity its reviewer gave it. Outside is therefore the LOUD side: the shorter the line, the more this contract covers and the more it quiets. An empty line is the widest coverage and the quietest gate, which is why `storybloq validate` warns about one. Silencing a category is a different mechanism and lives in `.story/config.json` under `recipeOverrides.blockingPolicy.neverBlock`.

The Outside line ships with three lens ids on it because the six principles above genuinely say nothing
about those subjects, and a finding is better passed through on its reviewer's judgement than capped for
naming no principle. Remove an entry to bring that subject under the contract; add one, as a category
string or a lens id, to take a subject out. Do not use this line to silence a category: a finding outside
the contract keeps the severity its reviewer gave it, which is louder, not quieter. Silencing lives in
`.story/config.json` under `recipeOverrides.blockingPolicy.neverBlock`.

Review id: R1
Review this full proposed Storybloq setup read-only. Return JSON {verdict,findings} matching supplied schema. Assess brief fidelity, coverage, usability, dependencies, feasibility, correctness/privacy, and verification. Do not create files.

Sources: brief.md Background: Riverside Community Garden, 40 plots, March-October seasons, volunteer coordinator, ~60 households.
brief.md First version must: applications with up to 3 preferred plots for coming season; coordinator allocates and moves unallocated applicants to waiting list in application order; gardeners see allocation and season dates; gardeners report problems for their plot, coordinator sees open/resolves; coordinator grid of all 40 plots showing holders.
brief.md Rules: household max one plot/season; prior-season holders who apply before 1 February allocated before new applicants; strictly first-come-first-served waiting list.
brief.md Constraints: phones, large text/plain language, contact details visible only to coordinator.
brief.md Later: payments/tool lending deferred.
Owner decisions: passwordless emailed one-time links; coordinator daily email listing new problem reports; no technology preference; use judgment for remaining questions.
Evidence: only brief.md exists; no code/manifests/tests/git/.story; no completion claims.

Product boundary: one garden, gardener and coordinator roles, 40 configurable plot labels, coordinator manual allocations respecting priority, no payments/tool lending, no multi-garden or automatic optimization.
Assumptions to approve: coordinator validates one household record and associated sign-in email(s), privately merges duplicate household registrations before allocation; returning status comes from verified prior-season holdings; one application per household/season, editable until coordinator closes applications, original submission timestamp retained; plot preferences optional (0-3 distinct plots), not guaranteed. Before-1-Feb means strictly before local midnight Feb 1 in configured garden timezone, no inference of geographical timezone. Coordinator configures exact season dates within March-October, timezone, daily digest time, and verifies prior-year roster before opening applications. Eligible returning applicants form first allocation group; within it chronological order. Other applicants chronological next. Coordinator may reject invalid/withdrawn applications with recorded reason, but cannot skip an eligible pending returner to allocate a new applicant. Waiting list uses original submission timestamp plus stable sequence tie-break; offers to next person only, no automated offer expiration. No active offer implies next promotion may proceed; offered household accepting allocates atomically, declining removes it from queue with recorded reason. Household/plot uniqueness enforced transactionally. No empty daily digest; daily emails list reports created since last successfully delivered cutoff, including those resolved since creation; retry doesn't silently omit reports. Provider uncertain delivery may produce duplicate email, never claim exactly-once external delivery.

Proposed architecture decision deferred to A1: choose language/framework/hosting/email provider supporting relational transactions, expiring single-use auth tokens, and scheduled jobs. No vendor commitment in setup; metadata Plotbook/generic/language TBD. Work is demonstrable without choosing vendor now. Deployment credentials and verified sending domain belong to owner during A1; missing them blocks delivery/release only, local fake mail remains possible.

Milestones after default p0:
M1 Foundation and access: household registration, sign-in, privacy, owner-reviewed phone journey.
M2 Seasonal allocation: applications, ordered allocation/waitlist, own allocation and coordinator map.
M3 Problem handling: reports/resolution and daily email.
M4 Release acceptance: end-to-end checks, backup/recovery, owner demonstration.

Every implementation ticket below uses complete template. References are brief headings above and owner decisions. IDs are planning labels, replaced with returned Storybloq IDs after approval.
A1 Establish application and verification tooling.
Outcome: a developer can run and verify Plotbook, enabling all brief outcomes.
Scope: choose/document stack, relational database, hosting/job/mail adapters; app skeleton, migrations, representative synthetic fixtures, test/build scripts, local fake email. Excludes: product workflows.
Acceptance: documented clean setup, smoke test, build, test collection, development readiness endpoint, chosen real email/job integration prerequisites recorded.
Behaviour: clear missing-config messages; no live secrets in files; startup failures actionable.
Verification: documented clean setup and passing smoke/build during implementation, never run during Storybloq setup. Prerequisites: none. Assumptions: technology selection delegated; choices recorded before dependent implementation.
A2 Household, season and plot records.
Outcome: coordinator can prepare trusted allocation data, from brief Background/Rules.
Scope: 40 plots, household/email membership, coordinator role bootstrap, prior season holdings import with validation/preview, season dates/timezone and cutoff, digest schedule; audited duplicate-household merge before allocation. Excludes: public contact directory.
Acceptance: exactly 40 unique plot records; duplicate household/email conflicts require resolution; holdings trustworthy; household and plot uniqueness per season enforced in database; coordinator approves initial roster and required seasonal configuration before opening.
Behaviour: explain invalid rows; atomic imports/merges; no partial corruption; accessible forms.
Verification: constraints, invalid import, merge, access-control and timezone-boundary tests. Prerequisites: A1. Assumptions: coordinator is final authority on household identity; synthetic data during development.
A3 Passwordless sign-in and role privacy.
Outcome: gardeners sign in by emailed one-time link, from owner; contacts stay coordinator-only from Constraints.
Scope: request/redeem links, sessions/signout, gardener household association, coordinator-only administration; unknown emails enter pending household registration for coordinator validation before applying. Excludes: passwords/social login.
Acceptance: single-use expiring hashed tokens; safe redirect; request rate limits and neutral responses; no contacts in gardener responses/markup/logs; gardener sees own records only; coordinator role cannot be self-assigned.
Behaviour: accessible mobile states, expired/used link retry, delivery failure recovery, no account enumeration.
Verification: replay/expiry/concurrent redemption and cross-household authorization tests, fake-mail end-to-end flow. Prerequisites: A1,A2. Assumptions: initial coordinator bootstrapped out of band; pending registrations clearly explained.
A4 Phone journey prototype.
Outcome: owner can inspect plain-language large-text application/allocation/report journeys, from Constraints.
Scope: navigable prototype with synthetic fixtures, keyboard/focus, labels, readable type and reflow. Excludes: production writes.
Acceptance: application/preferences, waiting/allocated, report submission, coordinator allocation/map/problem screens have empty/loading/error states; usable narrow phone viewport and zoom.
Behaviour: accessible feedback and recovery; no reliance on color alone.
Verification: keyboard/zoom/mobile walkthrough. Prerequisites: A1. Assumptions: visual style delegated.
C1 Checkpoint: phone journey and household onboarding.
Question: Does the prototype make applying/signing in/reporting clear, and is coordinator household validation practical?
Artifact: A4 prototype plus A2/A3 household/onboarding demonstration.
Dependencies: A2,A3,A4. Gates A5,A9 only; backend allocation A6 can proceed.

A5 Seasonal applications.
Outcome: gardener applies with up to three preferred plots, from First version 1.
Scope: coming-season application, 0-3 unique valid preferences, editing while open, original immutable ordering timestamp/sequence, duplicate submission protection and confirmation. Excludes: guarantees of chosen plot.
Acceptance: verified household can submit once per season; old submissions preserved across edits; closed seasons refuse new writes; invalid/duplicate preferences explained.
Behaviour: accessible loading/error/empty/success; retry does not create duplicates.
Verification: phone journey, 0/3/4 preferences, concurrent retry, season closure and edit-order tests. Prerequisites: A2,A3,C1. Assumptions: 0 preferences permitted; edits until close.
A6 Allocation and queue domain logic.
Outcome: coordinator allocations uphold Rules.
Scope: priority eligibility from prior holdings and cutoff; transactionally unique household/plot assignments; eligibility-aware selection; chronological waiting queue; offers/acceptance/decline/withdrawal and explicit invalid application rejection with audit. Excludes: automated optimization or auto-expiring offers.
Acceptance: before-cutoff returners precede new applicants; timestamps at cutoff in correct zone tested; queue always original submission order regardless returner status; no skipping queue on promotion; no double allocations or multiple active offers from retries/concurrency; invalid/withdrawn applications excluded with reason.
Behaviour: stale-state conflicts explain and refresh; rejected operations leave data unchanged.
Verification: table-driven rule tests including previous-season nonholder, cutoff equality, late returner, tied submissions, concurrent claims/offers. Prerequisites: A2. Assumptions: late returners treated with other applicants; preferred plot not required.
A7 Coordinator allocation workspace and 40-plot map.
Outcome: coordinator reviews applications, allocates and waitlists, and sees all holders in grid, from First version 2/5.
Scope: filters/priority indicators, explicit valid allocation actions, bulk move remaining applicants to ordered queue, offer/accept/decline controls, accessible map/list alternative, audit view. Excludes: contacts on gardener screens.
Acceptance: grid always 40 plots; current holder or vacancy identified; unauthorized requests rejected server-side; promotion follows A6; coordinator can see contact data and only valid actions.
Behaviour: readable mobile map/list, loading/no-applications/errors; concurrent change refresh.
Verification: role/API/UI tests and 41+ competing applications across 40 plots. Prerequisites: A3,A5,A6,A4.
Assumptions: coordinator records acceptance/decline after contacting gardener.
A8 Gardener allocation and queue status.
Outcome: gardener sees own allocation and exact dates from First version 3.
Scope: own plot, season dates, application pending/waiting/offered/allocated/declined states with clear next step. Excludes: other households' identities or contacts.
Acceptance: updates reflect coordinator actions; dates match season; no other household data returned.
Behaviour: understandable empty/loading/error/retry and keyboard/phone support.
Verification: state-transition journeys and cross-household tests. Prerequisites: A3,A5,A6,C1. Assumptions: contact coordinator for questions.
C2 Checkpoint: allocation milestone.
Criteria: demonstrate returner priority, strict chronological queue, 40-plot map, uniqueness and gardener allocation dates using synthetic sample season.
Artifact: A7/A8 working demo and A6 test evidence.
Dependencies: A7,A8. Gates C3 release acceptance only; problem work independent.

A9 Plot problem reporting.
Outcome: allocated gardener reports a plot problem, from First version 4.
Scope: plain text report tied server-side to household's allocated plot/season, confirmation and own report status. Excludes: attachments/chat.
Acceptance: nonallocated households cannot submit against others' plots; description validated; retries do not duplicate; creation timestamp recorded.
Behaviour: no-allocation guidance; accessible submit/success/error/retry; malicious text escaped.
Verification: authorization, validation, duplicate submission and phone journey tests. Prerequisites: A3,A6,C1.
Assumptions: report must relate to an active allocation; historical reports retained privately after season end.
A10 Coordinator problem resolution.
Outcome: coordinator views open problems and marks resolved, from First version 4.
Scope: open/resolved lists with plot/time, detail, mark resolved and audit timestamp; server-side role checks. Excludes: general messaging.
Acceptance: new report appears open; resolution removes from open view and updates gardener view; no public exposure.
Behaviour: accessible empty/loading/error states, idempotent resolution and stale-update recovery.
Verification: gardener-to-coordinator-to-resolved flow and authorization tests. Prerequisites: A9.
Assumptions: resolved reports retained; reopening deferred.
A11 Reliable daily report email.
Outcome: coordinator gets one daily email listing new reports, from owner.
Scope: authenticated scheduled job, configured garden-local schedule, durable report cutoff and delivery tracking, retry/deduplication, sanitized email content, provider failure visibility. Excludes: per-report email/SMS.
Acceptance: one scheduled digest per nonempty day; includes each newly created report even if since resolved; empty days no email; job retries/concurrency do not produce separate digest records; failed send preserves pending data; delayed runs cover backlog; email links require login.
Behaviour: outage/retry shown to coordinator; no secrets/contact leakage; external uncertain-delivery duplicate risk documented and provider idempotency used where available.
Verification: fake clock/provider tests for empty day, daylight-saving schedule, outage/retry, overlapping jobs, cutoff edge and resolved-new reports; staging real-email check. Prerequisites: A1,A9,A10.
Assumptions: chosen provider and credentials available for staging; daily time set by coordinator.

A12 Release verification and recovery.
Outcome: dependable first version can be demonstrated, from all requirements/Constraints.
Scope: end-to-end role journeys, accessibility/mobile checks, email/job staging validation, backup/restore drill, migration/restart checks, privacy/security verification, operator guide and deployment/rollback procedure. Excludes: invented load SLA or compliance claims.
Acceptance: all mapped requirements proven, backup restored, no cross-household/contact leak, setup/digest failure recovery documented, daily job configured; no real resident data required for tests.
Behaviour: operator sees actionable failures; restore never silently overwrites production.
Verification: recorded tests plus keyboard/zoom/phone walkthrough, staging deployment/mail and restore evidence. Prerequisites: A7,A8,A10,A11.
Assumptions: production credentials/domain supplied before launch; general personal data retention policy owner-visible and configurable before launch.
C3 Checkpoint: first-version acceptance.
Criteria: owner accepts full gardener/coordinator journey and map against every brief requirement and sign-in/digest decisions, confirms timezone/dates/household roster and production operational settings.
Artifact: staging application, A12 evidence, operating guide.
Dependencies: A12,C2. Gates deployment to production; no production deployment authorized by setup.

Coverage: apply/preference A5; allocation/waitlist A6/A7; own allocation/dates A8; report/resolution A9/A10; map A7; household uniqueness/returner priority/FCFS A2/A6; phones/plain language/large text A4/C1 and all UI tickets/A12; contacts A3/A7/A8/A12; links A3; daily email A11; 40 plots/season A2; payments/tool lending explicitly deferred.
Inventory: 17 tickets: A1-A12 plus A? Count carefully: A1,A2,A3,A4,C1,A5,A6,A7,A8,C2,A9,A10,A11,A12,C3 = 15 tickets (12 implementation + 3 checkpoints), four planned milestones plus default p0. No completed tickets/imported issues.
M1 A1-A4,C1; M2 A5-A8,C2; M3 A9-A11; M4 A12,C3.
Immediate: A1; A4 and A2 after A1, independently. Checkpoints are ordinary tickets; stage-1 software does not enforce human approval gates.
Governance on approval: AGENTS.md purpose/scope/architecture TBD/decisions/assumptions, RULES.md domain/privacy/transaction constraints and TDD for business logic, REVIEW.md exact supplied contract. No existing files overwritten.
Quality level: Full pipeline because allocation business rules and scheduled workflow. All four recipe stages explicitly disabled until tooling exists; proposed commands pending: WRITE_TESTS and TEST \"TBD in A1: selected stack test command\"; BUILD \"TBD in A1: selected stack build/check command\"; VERIFY \"TBD in A1: development server and readiness URL\". A1 establishes them, later configuration enables the approved stages once evidenced.
Git: initialize repo; ignore .story/snapshots/, .story/sessions/, .story/status.json. No import from GitHub. No install/build/test/dev runs during setup.
On explicit package approval only: initialize .story, create milestones/tickets, wire dependencies, governance/git, validate state, snapshot, initial handover and setup note capturing coverage/decisions/pending commands. No setup writes before approval.
STORYBLOQ_PLAN"

Plotbook’s proposed setup contains **15 tickets across four milestones**, plus Storybloq’s default Setup phase. It covers all five first-version capabilities, emailed sign-in links, and the daily coordinator email. Payments and tool lending remain deferred.

Phases are milestones; tickets are specific work items. The labels below are planning references—Storybloq will assign ticket IDs when created.

**Milestone 1: Foundation and access**

Each implementation ticket will contain scope, exclusions, observable acceptance conditions, failure behaviour, verification, prerequisites, and assumptions. Checkpoints are ordinary tickets: **Storybloq does not enforce human approval automatically.**

**Assumptions included for approval**

- The coordinator validates household registrations before applications, preventing duplicate household allocations.
- Preferences are optional, distinct, and not guaranteed. Editing preserves the original application order.
- Returning-gardener priority applies to initial allocation; the waiting list remains strictly chronological.
- The coordinator configures exact season dates, garden timezone, and daily email time.
- Empty daily emails are suppressed. Delivery failures retain reports for retry.
- Technology selection is delegated to A1; no provider purchase or production deployment is included.

- Project metadata: **Plotbook**, type **generic**, language **TBD in A1**.
